activity.role: Māori spiritual leader and Parihaka nonviolent resistance co-leader
activity.role_display_name_ko: 마오리 종교 지도자·파리하카 비폭력 저항 공동 지도자
activity.notes: Te Whiti o Rongomai and Tohu Kākahi co-led the Parihaka nonviolent resistance. On 5 November 1881, Crown forces invaded the settlement and arrested both leaders. The polity here denotes their Māori political-religious community, not any office in the New Zealand colonial government, a pan-Māori monarchy or solitary leadership; Activity is a single dated event point.

sources.title: Te Whiti-o-Rongomai III, Erueti — Dictionary of New Zealand Biography / Te Ara
sources.citation_text: Te Ara documents the 5 November 1881 invasion and arrest of Te Whiti and Tohu at Parihaka.

sources.title: 1880s — New Zealand Police Museum
sources.citation_text: New Zealand Police identifies Te Whiti and Tohu as joint leaders of Parihaka and the 1881 peaceful response to the armed force.

sources.title: Te Whiti — NZHistory (Manatū Taonga)
sources.citation_text: The New Zealand Ministry for Culture and Heritage corroborates the co-leadership, 1881 arrest and later return.
